newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end up in slow trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end up in slow trading.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended slightly up in slow trading on Monday on speculative buying, traders said.
The most active May 1997 contract ended at an intra-day high of 21,590 yuan ($2,602) per tonne, rising 110 yuan. It opened at 21,400 and hit a low of 21,360.
February rose 70 to 21,210, March 70 to 21,310, April 90 to 21,480, and June 100 to 21,600.
Combined volume fell to 17,030 tonnes from 30,030.
Traders said many investors stayed on the sidelines today due to a lack of market-moving news.
"Trading interest was not very strong with the approach of the Chinese new year holiday," one trader said.
"But market sentiment was steady with some investors preferring to offset their positions," he added.
Traders said the general outlook for copper was not clear despite the optimistic attitude of some analysts.
"Fundamentals and technical charts have actually improved since the beginning of the year, as many analysts expected, but the long-term trend has not changed," a second trader said.
Analysts said they expected copper to continue moving in a narrow range in the next few days.
Aluminium ended mostly up. February rose 100 to 15,000, March 100 to 15,300, and April was unchanged at 15,600.
Combined volume rose to 1,190 tonnes from 560.
